title: Support runtime fields in synthetic source

timeline.message: Support runtime fields in synthetic source
timeline.author: Kostas Krikellas

+      reason: Runtime mappings support was added in 7.12

+  - do:

+            _source:

+          aggs:
+            field3:
+              terms:
+                field: field3
+
+  - length: { aggregations.field3.buckets: 0 }
+
+  - do:
+      bulk:
+        index: index1
+        refresh: true
+        body: |
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "A", "field2": "B" }
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "A", "field2": "B" }
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "C", "field2": "D" }
+
+  - do:
+      search:
+        body:
+          size: 0
+          runtime_mappings:
+            field3:
+              type: keyword
+              script:
+                source: "emit(params._source.field1 + params._source.field2)"
+          aggs:
+            field3:
+              terms:
+                field: field3
+
+  - length: { aggregations.field3.buckets: 2 }
+  - match: { aggregations.field3.buckets.0.key: AB }
+  - match: { aggregations.field3.buckets.0.doc_count: 2 }

+  - match: { aggregations.field3.buckets.1.doc_count: 1 }
+
+
+---

+  - skip:
+      version: " - 7.11.99"
+      reason: Runtime mappings support was added in 7.12
+
+  - do:
+      indices.create:
+        index: index1
+        body:
+          mappings:
+            _source:
+              mode: synthetic
+            properties:
+              field1:
+                type: double
+              field2:
+                type: double
+
+  - do:
+      search:
+        body:
+          size: 0
+          runtime_mappings:
+            field3:
+              type: double
+              script:
+                source: "emit(params._source.field1 + params._source.field2)"
+          aggs:
+            field3:
+              terms:
+                field: field3
+
+  - length: { aggregations.field3.buckets: 0 }
+
+  - do:
+      bulk:
+        index: index1
+        refresh: true
+        body: |
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "1", "field2": "2" }
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "1", "field2": "2" }
+          {"index":{}}
+          { "field1": "3", "field2": "4" }
+
+  - do:
+      search:
+        body:
+          size: 0
+          runtime_mappings:
+            field3:
+              type: double
+              script:
+                source: "emit(params._source.field1 + params._source.field2)"
+          aggs:
+            field3:
+              terms:
+                field: field3
+
+  - length: { aggregations.field3.buckets: 2 }
+  - match: { aggregations.field3.buckets.0.key: 3.0 }
+  - match: { aggregations.field3.buckets.0.doc_count: 2 }

timeline.body:
This is needed to use runtime fields in TSDS that use synthetic source by default.

Fixes #98287

timeline.body: Hi @kkrik-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

This is going to decompress a whole stored field block on every document, potentially re-doing the same work over and over again.  If you want to enable this then I think we need to look again at the SourceLoader.Synthetic implementation, and indeed the SourceLoader API, as it expects to be able to load a complete set of docIds ahead of time and really isn't designed to handle very large numbers of docs.

reply.body:
Thanks Alan. I assume we want to decompress the block once and reuse the values we get for fetching docs later.

Do you have any good pointers on how to make these changes? I'll take a closer look to SourceLoader internals too.

Yes, we ideally want to have just a single LeafStoredFieldLoader and SourceLoader.Leaf per segment.  I think you want a new SourceProvider implementation that's tailored specifically for synthetic source, and you'll want to adjust the various implementations of SyntheticFieldLoader.DocValuesLoader to fall back to doc-by-doc loading if the passed in docids array is `null`.
Updated, is this closer to what you had in mind? Thanks.

timeline.body: I think you'll need to call `leafLoader.advanceTo(doc)` here?
I don't think `ctx` can ever be null?
I think you can just remove this bit of the test; maybe add some testing that the Source returned earlier has the expected value?

reply.body: I removed this part, but it's tricky to get a unittest that evaluates a script - `TestRuntimeField` doesn't return actual values.. We get more coverage here from the yaml test, but I can try to subclass TestRuntimeField (or something along these lines) if you insist.
I think you can just check that `Source.asMap().get("unloaded").get(0)` returns what you expect?  No need for scripting, just look at the constructed `Source` directly.
I wish, `asMap` is null, I think we're getting into the "sourceLoader.requiredStoredFields().isEmpty()" path..
That sounds like a bug?  It should be reconstructing the source for you, surely?

Oh hang on, no I see what the issue is, you have an empty Mapping so there's nothing for it to base its reconstruction on.  I think you can add a field to the mapping, make sure that it's added as either or a stored field or a doc value field to the MemoryIndex, and then check the reconstruction.  In fact it's probably worth checking both types of reconstruction (stored field & doc value).
I added a field to the mapping, but I still see an empty `storedFieldLoaders` in `SourceLoader.Synthetic`.. Updated the test, will keep looking.

I get to see `asMap` containing a keyword but not the runtime field. I think the reason is that runtime fields are not added to the fields that the SyntheticFieldLoader tracks [1,2]. I can see in [2] that `extra` contains the SourceFieldMapper and `mappers` contains the KeywordFieldMapper; the runtime field is tracked under member `runtimeFields` but not added here..

I committed my latest changes, any further help here is appreciated.

[1] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/Mapping.java#L128
[2]  https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/ObjectMapper.java#L602

Synthetic source works by rebuilding the source document using other index structures, but runtime fields don't have any index structures so they will indeed not work here.

I think this might be better tested if we can hook it into `MapperServiceTestCase`, specifically the `syntheticSource()` method on line 721.  If you can rewrite that method to use this new SourceProvider to load the Source, then it will get tested for every mapping type.
